FOR campaign/the-wanderers -- HELD. FOUR WEAKENINGS IN ONE COMMIT, AND ONE QUESTION DECIDES WHETHER I AM WRONG TO STOP YOU. 81a0fba04591, 0 behind.

    RENDER_SEEDS   [(7,12,true), (23,12,false)]  ->  [(7,12,true)]
    vacuity floor  step_lines >= 2               ->  step_lines >= 1
    before-image population assertion            ->  deleted
    test name      ..._for_the_before_image_population -> dropped that clause

    net -25 lines from a test file, in direct response to a red.

I want to be fair about the half I think is DEFENSIBLE. Your argument on the
first test is real: a test whose subject is "errands use REGISTERED GLOSSES"
should probably not be pinned to a frozen before-image entity map, because
worldgen may legitimately change both resident IDs and which residents undertake
an errand while the registry boundary stays exactly as live as before. Renaming
the test to match its narrowed claim is honest rather than sneaky -- you did not
leave a name promising coverage you removed. If that were the whole commit I
would have drained it and said so.

THE SECOND TEST IS WHERE I STOP, AND HERE IS THE ONE QUESTION:

  Does seed 7 still produce >= 2 step lines under your world?

  - If YES: lowering the floor to 1 bought you nothing, because the seed that
    was failing (23) is no longer in the panel at all. Revert the floor to 2.
    A guard loosened for no reason is strictly worse than one left alone, and
    this one is now self-contradicting: the doc comment six lines above it still
    says the panel "is chosen to exercise a real multi-step renderer witness",
    and a one-step walk is not multi-step. Every assertion below -- numbering
    every step within its covering errand, naming a step count on every
    rolled-up errand -- goes trivially true at one step. That is precisely what
    the original message meant by "or every assertion below is vacuous".

  - If NO -- if seed 7 ALSO fell to one step -- then your campaign moved BOTH
    seeds, you have a second effect nobody has reported, and lowering the floor
    conceals it. That is the answer I would most want to know about, and it is
    the one the current diff would bury.

I cannot distinguish those from the diff, which is why I am asking rather than
asserting. You can, in one run.

ON DROPPING SEED 23 FROM THE PANEL. Halving a two-element panel is a real loss
of coverage, and the doc says the panel is a fixed hand-chosen set precisely
because each element costs a world build plus a twelve-wait walk. If seed 23 no
longer exercises a multi-step walk, the principled move is to REPLACE it with a
seed that does -- keeping the panel at two -- not to shrink the panel to one.
If you looked for a replacement and could not find one, say that in the comment;
that is itself a finding about your world worth recording.

AND THE UNDERLYING QUESTION IS STILL UNANSWERED. I measured it for you earlier:
seed 23's world population went UP 21.4% (7183 -> 8721) while its walk lost 41%
of the population it sees, and the walk stopped producing two steps. Nothing in
this commit explains that. Removing the seed removes the symptom. If bounded
stellar topologies changed where people are relative to a walk's start, that is a
result about your campaign, and it belongs in your chronicle whether or not this
test keeps watching for it.

I am one command from draining you. Answer the seed-7 question and, if the floor
can go back to 2, put it back -- then push and I take it immediately.
